1.note: This is an idiom that is used to introduce something that God told his prophets or his people. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 3:16. Alternate translation: [Yahweh spoke this message] or [Yahweh spoke these words]

2.note: See how you translated **Son of man** in [2:1](ta:02).

Yahweh is using **set your face to the sons of Ammon** as a common expression of the culture to mean “turn toward the sons of Ammon in order to oppose them.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [turn toward the sons of Ammon to oppose them]

Yahweh is speaking as if the Ammonite people, who were descended from Ammon, were Ammon’s **sons**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. This also occurs in verses 3, 5, and 10. Alternate translation: [the Ammonite people]

3.q: וְ⁠אָֽמַרְתָּ֙ לִ⁠בְנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן שִׁמְע֖וּ דְּבַר אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֑ה
3.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And you will tell the sons of Ammon to hear the word of the Lord Yahweh]

The Ammonites were using a phrase, **Aha**, that expresses a strong feeling of malicious joy. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Ha ha]

The expression **because it was profaned** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. The context indicates that the Babylonians did this. Alternate translation: [because the Babylonians profaned it]

The expression **because it was desolated** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. The context indicates that the Babylonians did this. Alternate translation: [because the Babylonians devastated it]
See how you translated **the house of Judah** in 4:6. This also occurs in verses 8 and 12.
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:4. This also occurs in verses 6, 8, 12, 13, 15, and 16.

4.note: Yahweh is using **the sons of the east** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the peoples who live in the desert to the east.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to the peoples of the eastern desert]

Yahweh is using **behold me giving you** as a common expression of the culture to mean that he was about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to give you]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **possession**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [so that they may possess you]

4.q: וְ⁠יִשְּׁב֤וּ טִירֽוֹתֵי⁠הֶם֙ בָּ֔⁠ךְ וְ⁠נָ֥תְנוּ בָ֖⁠ךְ מִשְׁכְּנֵי⁠הֶ֑ם
4.note: Here, **in you** represents “in your land.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And they will set their encampments in your land, and they will put their dwellings in your territory]

4.q: הֵ֚מָּה יֹאכְל֣וּ פִרְיֵ֔⁠ךְ וְ⁠הֵ֖מָּה יִשְׁתּ֥וּ חֲלָבֵֽ⁠ךְ
4.note: The pronoun **They** refers to the sons of the east. Yahweh repeats the pronoun for emphasis. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The sons of the east themselves will eat your fruit, and they themselves will drink your milk]

5.q: וְ⁠נָתַתִּ֤י אֶת רַבָּה֙ לִ⁠נְוֵ֣ה גְמַלִּ֔ים וְ⁠אֶת בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן לְ⁠מִרְבַּץ צֹ֑אן
5.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [And I will turn Rabbah and all the land of the sons of Ammon into nothing but pastureland for animals]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. The full thought would be “I will give the land belonging to the sons of Ammon as a resting place of flocks,” meaning he will turn their land into pastureland. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [I will make the land of the sons of Ammon into a resting place of flocks]

The word **you** is plural here because Yahweh is now addressing the Ammonite people, even though in the previous verses he used the singular form to address the nation of Ammon. So use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction. This also occurs in verses 7, 11, and 17.

6.note: Clapping the hand and stamping the foot were symbolic actions by which the Ammonites showed their malicious joy over the disaster that had come upon Israel. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of these actions in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [your clapping the hand and your stamping with the foot to celebrate the disaster that came on Israel]

Yahweh is using **contempt in the soul** as a common expression of the culture to mean “utter scorn.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you rejoiced with complete scorn]

7.note: Yahweh is using **behold me** as an expression that people of this culture would commonly use to mean that they were about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to stretch out my hand against you]

Here, **my hand** represents “my power.” Yahweh is referring to using his power to punish the Ammonites. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [behold, I have used my power against you]

The word **plunder** is a translation of a correction in the margin of the text that Hebrew scribes have recommended. The standard written text has a rare word here whose meaning is uncertain. You may want to follow this correction in your translation, as the ULT does, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area.

Yahweh is speaking of destroying the Ammonites as a nation as if he were going to **cut** them **off** from the other peoples. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will destroy you so that you are no longer one of the peoples]

8.q: יַ֗עַן אֲמֹ֤ר מוֹאָב֙ וְ⁠שֵׂעִ֔יר הִנֵּ֥ה כְּ⁠כָֽל הַ⁠גּוֹיִ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יְהוּדָֽה
8.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Because Moab and Seir have said that the house of Judah is just like all of the nations]

Here, **Moab and Seir** represent the people of Moab and Seir. Seir was another name for Edom. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the saying of the Moabites and the Edomites]

The point of this comparison is that just as **all of the nations** are ordinary peoples with no special god, so is **the house of Judah**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point . Alternate translation: [the house of Judah is an ordinary people with no special god, just as all of the nations are]

9.note: Yahweh is using **opening the shoulder of Moab** as a common expression of the culture to mean “leaving the frontier of Moab without defense.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [behold me leaving the border of Moab without defense]

Here Yahweh is speaking of Moab’s frontier as if it were the **end** of something. He means the border cities that marked the edge of Moab’s territory. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from its edge] or [from its border]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe the cities that were the **splendor** of the **land**, that is, the most splendid cities in Moab. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the most splendid cities in the land]
The words **Beth Jeshimoth**, **Baal Meon**, and **Kiriathaim** are the names of towns.

10.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [to the sons of the east, just as I opened the land of the sons of Ammon to them]
The pronoun **it** refers to the territory of Moab. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And I will give the territory of Moab as a possession]

Yahweh is using **will not be remembered among the nations** as a common expression of the culture to mean “will no longer exist as a people.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the sons of Ammon will no longer exist as a people among the nations]

The expression **will not be remembered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. The nations are the ones who will not remember them. Alternate translation: [will have no one who remembers them]

11.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **judgments**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And I will judge Moab]

12.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **doing**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Because of what Edom did]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. This also occurs in verse 15.

12.q: יַ֣עַן עֲשׂ֥וֹת אֱד֛וֹם בִּ⁠נְקֹ֥ם נָקָ֖ם & וְ⁠נִקְּמ֥וּ
12.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **vengeance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [because Edom violently repaid … and they violently repaid]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **became guilty** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [and they became very guilty]

The pronoun **they** refers to the Edomites, and the pronoun **them** refers to the people of Judah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the Edomites took vengeance on the people of Judah]

13.note: See how you translated these same phrases in verse 7. Alternate translation: [I will act with power against Edom to destroy] or [I will punish Edom and destroy]

Yahweh is referring to all of the living things in Edom by naming two major components, **man** and **beast**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and I will cut off from her every living thing]

Yahweh is referring to all of the land of Edom by naming two places at its extremes, **Teman** and **Dedan**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And I will make all of her land a waste, and throughout her territory]
The words **Teman** and **Dedan** are the names of places.

Here, **the sword** represents “warfare,” and **fall** means “die.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [they will die in battle]

14.note: See how you translated these same phrases in verse 12. Alternate translation: [And I will violently repay Edom … that I have violently repaid them]

Here, **by the hand of** represents “through the action of.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [through the actions of my people Israel]

The terms **anger** and **wrath** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [according to my great anger]
See how you translated **the declaration of the Lord Yahweh** in 5:11.

15.note: Yahweh is using **contempt in the soul** as a common expression of the culture to mean “utter scorn.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [with utter scorn]

15.q: יַ֛עַן עֲשׂ֥וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים בִּ⁠נְקָמָ֑ה וַ⁠יִּנָּקְמ֤וּ נָקָם֙
15.note: See how you translated these same phrases in verse 12. Alternate translation: [Because of what the Philistines did in anger]

16.note: Yahweh is using words with similar sounds for poetic effect. In the original language, the word for **cut off** sounds similar to the word for **Cherethites**. You may want to reproduce this effect if poetry in your language does this.
See how you translated these same phrases in verse 7. Alternate translation: [acting powerfully … and destroying]

Here, **the shore of the sea** represents “the people who live along the shore of the sea.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the remaining people who live along the shore of the sea]

17.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **rebukes** that are characterized by **wrath**. In this context, the rebukes are punishments. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with angry punishments]
